title: Build a compact five-minute composition plan
instructions: Continue from the E6 focus map about using a school-learned problem-solving method at a charity sale. Build a compact introduction–body–conclusion plan. The five-minute routine is a practice target, not an official exam allocation. Answer all six questions before viewing feedback.

parts.prompt: Which sequence uses the five-minute rehearsal routine most effectively?

options.text: Write a polished introduction; count its words; copy it neatly; then think of examples.
Check the task and focus; plan body jobs and evidence; sketch the introduction and conclusion; add relationship transitions; audit coverage.
List every possible idea; choose the longest; write the conclusion; ignore the task until the end.
Choose transitions first; add unrelated examples; write two controlling focuses; begin drafting.

choice_rationales.A: Polishing prose before planning the evidence consumes time and can hide missing requirements.
choice_rationales.B: This sequence moves from task control to the body route, frames it, connects it and checks it.
choice_rationales.C: An unlimited idea list and delayed task check create drift rather than a compact route.
choice_rationales.D: Transitions cannot repair unrelated evidence or competing central responses.

parts.hint: Choose the route that establishes task control before organising, connecting and checking the plan.
parts.correct_explanation: The effective routine protects the task contract and focus, plans the evidence-bearing body first, adds the frame and then audits the complete route.

parts.prompt: Which THREE notes belong in the introduction plan?

options.text: School learning: break a large problem into smaller parts.
Different life setting: organising a charity sale.
Focus: the method made decisions manageable and supported adaptation.
Draft a polished 120-word account of every stall before planning the body.
Introduce a second main claim that teamwork matters more than problem-solving.

choice_rationales.A: This identifies the school-learned method required by the task.
choice_rationales.B: This establishes the different area of life in which the method is applied.
choice_rationales.C: This gives the whole composition one controlling response.
choice_rationales.D: A compact plan records the opening's job rather than drafting a long paragraph.
choice_rationales.E: A competing central claim would split the response before the body begins.

parts.hint: Select the learning, application and controlling focus; leave drafting and competing claims out.
parts.correct_explanation: Together, the three notes establish what was learned, where it transferred and what the composition will demonstrate.

parts.prompt: Which note is the strongest plan for body paragraph one?

options.text: Job: initial planning. Evidence: divide publicity, supplies, prices and staffing; assign deadlines. Explain: separate tasks turned a confusing workload into manageable action.
Job: charity sale. Evidence: it was busy. Explain: it was interesting.
Write every sentence of the paragraph now and leave no time to plan the complication.
Job: prove teamwork is the only skill anyone needs. Evidence: several people attended.

choice_rationales.A: The note gives the paragraph one job, specific evidence and an explicit link to the focus.
choice_rationales.B: The general labels do not explain what happened or how the school learning mattered.
choice_rationales.C: Drafting one complete paragraph does not create a route for the whole response.
choice_rationales.D: This replaces the controlling focus and makes an unsupported absolute claim.

parts.hint: Look for a distinct paragraph job supported by concrete actions and a link-back.
parts.correct_explanation: The strongest note is compact but complete: it names the initial-planning job, supplies usable evidence and explains its significance.

parts.prompt: Which note best develops body paragraph two and connects it to paragraph one?

options.text: Secondly, the event continued. Add any facts that come to mind.
Repeat the publicity, supplies, prices and staffing list without a new paragraph job.
When conditions changed: rain moved stalls indoors. Rank urgent moving and safety tasks; reassign helpers. Explain: the same step-by-step method supported calm adaptation.
Change the topic to the history of school fundraising because it creates variety.

choice_rationales.A: A numbered connector and unspecified facts do not show a meaningful relationship.
choice_rationales.B: Repeating the first job prevents the composition from developing.
choice_rationales.C: The complication transition, new evidence and link-back extend the same controlling focus.
choice_rationales.D: Unrelated background creates topic drift instead of progression.

parts.hint: The second paragraph should signal the complication, add new evidence and preserve the same focus.
parts.correct_explanation: The plan progresses from initial organisation to adaptation and uses the changed conditions to make that relationship visible.

parts.prompt: Which note gives the conclusion the right job?

options.text: Summarise the insight: one clear part at a time reduced confusion and helped me adjust; transfer the method to future complex responsibilities.
Introduce a new story about winning a sports competition.
Copy the introduction exactly and add no reflection.
Claim that this method guarantees success in every situation.

choice_rationales.A: This closes the established focus and extends the learning credibly without adding a new main example.
choice_rationales.B: A new story belongs in a new composition, not the conclusion of this route.
choice_rationales.C: Mechanical repetition does not synthesise what the evidence showed.
choice_rationales.D: The absolute conclusion overstates what one example can prove.

parts.hint: Choose a conclusion that closes the existing response through insight rather than new evidence or overclaiming.
parts.correct_explanation: A useful conclusion returns to the demonstrated effect and shows a bounded future transfer of the same learning.

parts.prompt: Which complete plan is ready for drafting after the final audit?

options.text: Introduction: learning + charity-sale setting + focus. Body 1: initial division of tasks -> manageable plan. Transition: when conditions changed. Body 2: rain response and reprioritising -> calm adaptation. Conclusion: insight and credible future use. Audit: task, focus, distinct jobs, evidence and links all present.
Introduction: charity sales are fun. Body: list posters, shoes, food and weather. Conclusion: school is good.
Introduction: two different focuses. Body 1: polished but unsupported claim. Body 2: repeat it. Conclusion: add a new example.
Introduction only, written in full. Decide the body and conclusion while drafting.

choice_rationales.A: Every task element has a place, the body jobs develop one another and the transitions express real relationships.
choice_rationales.B: The details do not form an explanatory route or demonstrate transferred learning.
choice_rationales.C: Split focus, weak evidence, repetition and a late new idea all fail the audit.
choice_rationales.D: An introduction alone cannot guide or protect the complete response.

parts.hint: Use the audit: task coverage, one focus, distinct paragraph jobs, specific evidence, relationship transitions and a closing insight.
parts.correct_explanation: The complete plan supplies a compact route from task and focus through two developing body jobs to a conclusion, with every required audit check visible.
